definition: The file in which Terraform records which real resources correspond to the code. Keep it in a remote backend - on Azure, a storage account with blob-lease locking, versioning and private access - with one state per environment and layer. It often contains secrets, so protect it like one; a local or unlocked state file is how environments get corrupted.
example: Each shop environment's GitHub-organisation Terraform state lives in its own container in a private, versioned storage account.

definition: A reusable piece of infrastructure code with parameters and outputs, called from other templates. Modules are versioned and shared through a registry, so every environment and team builds resources the same way. Terraform has the equivalent concept.
example: workloads/shop/main.bicep calls the App Service plan and web app modules with different parameters for dev and production.

definition: A preview of exactly what a deployment would create, modify or delete, run before applying it: az deployment ... what-if for Bicep and ARM, terraform plan for Terraform. Posting it on every infrastructure pull request lets reviewers catch destructive changes - including renames, which delete and recreate a resource.
example: The what-if comment shows '1 to delete: sqldb-orders-prod' after a rename, and the pull request is stopped.

definition: Any difference between what infrastructure code declares and what is actually deployed, usually from manual changes. Prevent it with read-only production access, Azure Policy and deployment stack deny settings; detect it with scheduled what-if or plan runs; resolve it by updating the code or re-applying it.
example: A nightly what-if against production flags an NSG rule opened by hand during an incident.

definition: Microsoft-maintained Bicep and Terraform modules for Azure services, published in public registries, built to follow Well-Architected defaults and kept up to date. Starting from them avoids hand-writing and maintaining the same resource definitions in every organisation.
example: The shop's templates reference br/public:avm/res/web/site for App Service rather than a hand-written module.
